statement: The reviewed legal benchmark paper states that retrieval-oriented legal benchmarks assume a normatively stable corpus and do not assess whether retrieved provisions remain in force or have been superseded, amended or repealed; that static legal benchmarks do not capture the amendment-driven character of statutory law; that current architectures lack the temporal logic to determine whether a retrieved provision remains in force; and that its own items are built from pairs of EUR-Lex document passages and their associated relations.

evidence.quote: Still, it assumes the underlying corpus is normatively stable and does not assess whether retrieved provisions remain in force or have been superseded, amended, or repealed.
It does not capture the amendment-driven and time-sensitive character of statutory law that governs legal reasoning.
